Repeated validation selection can overfit a finite validation set; ordinary confidence intervals do not remove winner-selection bias ([Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). Practical implication: predeclare a small ablation table, comparison contrasts, stopping rules and GPU allocations; log every attempted configuration. Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, BERT4Rec, splits and evaluator fixed. Treat selected validation gains as exploratory; reserve held-out evaluation for the frozen choice.

For paired uncertainty, retain each model’s per-user hit indicator on identical candidates. Compute category differences as mean paired hit differences, then average the four differences equally. Bootstrap paired users within each category and recompute the macro difference for a 95% interval; report category deltas and discordant hit counts alongside it. Bootstrap/randomization methods have supporting recommendation-evaluation research ([source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.02461)). One changed hit moves category HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 points. These intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on trained models and candidate sets—not training-seed variability, negative-sampling variability or selection bias. With 99 sampled negatives, conclusions concern this pinned benchmark; sampled rankings can reverse full-catalog comparisons ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)).

Suggested budget design: baseline plus separate masking, recency-sampling, training-negative-count and loss changes, followed by targeted interaction checks. Single-factor contrasts identify effects at the baseline but miss interactions ([NIST](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/pri/section2/pri212.htm)). Keep evaluation negatives fixed; specify loss normalization when changing training-negative count. Cap total work at 43,200 GPU-seconds, including failures and diagnostics; four slots reduce elapsed time, not GPU cost. Reserve budget for complete four-category comparisons; report compute costs and avoid attributing bundled changes to individual components.
